title: Grade 11 Mathematics — Trigonometric Functions & Complex Numbers
description: Trigonometric Functions and Complex Numbers and Quadratic Equations practice questions
subject: mathematics

questions.question: The value of sin(−30°) is:
questions.explanation: sin is an odd function: sin(−θ) = −sin θ. sin(−30°) = −sin(30°) = −1/2.

questions.question: The period of the function f(x) = sin(2x) is:
questions.explanation: Period of sin(nx) = 2π/n. For sin(2x): period = 2π/2 = π.

questions.question: The identity sin²x + cos²x =
questions.explanation: The Pythagorean identity: sin²x + cos²x = 1 for all real x. This is the most fundamental trigonometric identity.

questions.question: sin(A + B) =
options: sin A cos B − cos A sin B
sin A cos B + cos A sin B
cos A cos B − sin A sin B
questions.explanation: sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B. This is a fundamental compound angle formula.

questions.question: The value of cos(60°) + sin(30°) is:
In which quadrant is sin positive and cos negative?
questions.explanation: In Quadrant II (90° to 180°): sin is positive, cos is negative, tan is negative. Mnemonic: ASTC (All, Sin, Tan, Cos) — All positive in I, Sin in II, Tan in III, Cos in IV.

questions.question: The principal solution of sin x = 1/2 in [0, 2π] is:
questions.explanation: sin x = 1/2 in [0, 2π]: x = π/6 (Q1) and x = π − π/6 = 5π/6 (Q2). Both are principal solutions.

questions.question: The formula for sin(2A) is:
questions.explanation: Double angle formula: sin(2A) = 2 sin A cos A. This is derived from sin(A+A) = sin A cos A + cos A sin A.

questions.question: The value of i² is:
questions.explanation: i = √(−1) is the imaginary unit. By definition, i² = −1. This is the foundational property of complex numbers.

questions.question: The modulus of the complex number 3 + 4i is:
The conjugate of the complex number 2 + 3i is:
questions.explanation: The conjugate of a + bi is a − bi. The conjugate of 2 + 3i is 2 − 3i. Conjugates have equal real parts and opposite imaginary parts.

questions.question: The argument (angle) of the complex number −1 + i is:
questions.explanation: For −1 + i: real part negative, imaginary part positive → Q2. |arg| = arctan(1/1) = π/4. Angle = π − π/4 = 3π/4.

questions.question: The sum of a complex number and its conjugate (z + z̄) is:
questions.explanation: If z = a + bi, then z̄ = a − bi. z + z̄ = (a+bi) + (a−bi) = 2a = 2 × Re(z). The sum is always real.

questions.question: The quadratic equation x² + 1 = 0 has roots:
questions.explanation: x² + 1 = 0 → x² = −1 → x = ±√(−1) = ±i. This is why complex numbers were invented — to solve equations with no real roots.
